text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM convinces unions that the airline's support services will not be outsourced as much as they fear. (p1)
- Consortium led by engineering group Stork gets a one billion guilder order from NAM. (p1)
- Management and works council of export credit insurer NCM reach compromise on restructuring plan. (p1)
- Real competition between Dutch PTT and its rivals slowed down by technical issues. (p1)
- Food concern CSM books eight percent higher net in 1996 book year ending September 30. (p3)
- Builders consortium Ballast Nedam and HBG in race for building super stadium for German soccer club Schalke 04. (p3)
- Maintenance companies in U.S. state of Florida file a multi-million dollar claim against Oce Printing Systems, a Oce van der Grinten subsidiary. (p5)
- Manufacturing output in the Netherlands is two percent higher in Q3 than in a year-earlier period. (p7)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Car and telecom dealer Pon Holding takes over lease company Gunco from ING Lease. (p2)
- Buying CD's via the Internet no longer cheap since tighter control imposed on imports. (p3)
- Owners of small businesses in the engineering sector want to put a stop to wage increases. (p6)
- Shareholders lobby group VEB criticises temp agency Content for buying back shares. (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Foreign affairs minister Hans van Mierlo has faith in Dutch EU presidency starting January. (p9)
- ABN Amro bank chief J. Kalff warns his Belgian colleagues of effects of European single currency. (p37)
- Sales of building materials will continue to grow by 1.6 pct each year until 2000. (p37)
- Contractors group HAM orders a Dfl 95 million trailing suction dredger from Verolme shipyard. (p39)
TROUW
- Financial services group ING to start up telephone banking unit ING Direct in Canada at the beginning of next year. (p7)
- ABN Amro bank closes subscription of new shares in industrial gas firm Hoek Loos earlier. (p24)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Unions' strike ultimatum to Dutch Railways runs out Sunday at midnight. (p1)
- Dutch businesses using Internet say it is too slow, inconvenient and has too few users - research. (p13)
